01.title: The Universal Father
01.001.h3: 1. The Universal Father: The Origin of All Creation
01.002.h4: 1) The Absolute Center of All Things
01.003.p: The origin and center of all creation is the Universal Father [1:0.1]. Enlightened worlds recognize and worship him as the eternal creator and infinite upholder of all creation [1:0.3]. He is the creator, controller, and infinite sustainer of the universes of universes [1:0.1]. Countless inhabited worlds were formed for intelligent creatures who could know God, accept his divine affection, and love him in return [1:0.2].
01.004.h4: 2) The Starting Point of the True Concept of God
01.005.p: A true understanding of the Universal Father begins not with polytheism but with the concept of one God [1:0.1]. This eternal and infinite being is the primal reality of the spiritual world [1:2.1], the source of truth in the domain of mind, and the one who permeates the entire realm of matter [1:2.1]. He is neither like a person nor a machine; he is the universal spirit, eternal truth, infinite reality, and the personality of a Father [1:2.1]. God is not merely a human ideal or the projection of man’s highest wishes [1:2.2]; he is transcendent reality, a savior, and a loving Father [1:2.2].
01.006.h3: 2. The Inner Presence That Reveals God: The Thought Adjuster
01.007.h4: 1) God Cannot Be Proved by Logic
01.008.p: We cannot prove the Father by scientific experiment or logical reasoning [1:7.5]. He is known only within the realm of human experience, owing to the divine indwelling presence—the spiritual companion known as the Thought Adjuster [5:0.1].
01.009.h4: 2) The Divine Work of the Adjuster
01.010.p: This divine Adjuster is the mystery monitor sent from the central dwelling place of the eternal presence [1:3.1]. He dwells within us and assists in the evolution of our immortal soul [1:3.6]. The Adjuster’s indwelling is one of the deepest and most unfathomable mysteries concerning the Universal Father [1:4.1]. Because this unseen fragment of God lives within us, our very bodies become temples of God [1:4.2]. To know the Father, we need look no further than thoughtful meditation upon the spiritual reality within us [5:0.1].
01.013.p: This eternal God has given us one majestic and universal mandate: “⟦Q 1:0.3⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect⟦/Q⟧” [1:0.3]. Although finite beings cannot attain absolute perfection in an infinite sense [1:0.5], we can attain final and complete goals in every finite aspect of divine will, moral motive, and God-consciousness [1:0.5].
01.015.p: Striving for God’s perfection is the first duty and highest aspiration of all creatures [1:0.4]. This noble quest to find the God of the universe is the supreme adventure for all inhabitants of the worlds of time and space [1:0.6].
01.016.h3: 4. The Personality and Omnipotence of the Universal Father
01.017.h4: 1) The Personal Nature of the Father
01.018.p: The Father exercises infinite power, wisdom, and love toward all creation [3:2.1], 3:2.6, but the most significant truth is that he is a personal being [1:5.7]. He is the source and upholder of all personality [5:6.1], the infinite personality [1:5.7]. He loves us, can be known by us, and is a true creator personality who can be our friend [1:5.8]. We call him “Father” because we recognize ourselves as his children [1:1.1].
01.020.p: The Universal Father is unlimited and infinite in all his attributes [2:1.6]. His omnipresence is unrestricted by space [3:1.1]~2. “Do I not fill heaven and earth?” [3:1.2] He is continually present in the hearts of all his far-flung creation [3:1.2].
01.021.p: His omniscience includes awareness of all creature thought [3:3.2], and his knowledge is further complemented by the descending divine Sons and the indwelling Adjuster [3:3.3].
01.022.h3: 5. The Essence of God: Love and Mercy
01.024.p: At the core of this vast being is love [2:5.12]. God’s love is the natural affection of a Father [2:5.10]. His love functions in unity with divine wisdom and the perfect nature of the Universal Father [2:5.10]. His personal attitude always reveals divine affection [2:5.10], and his mercy endures forever.
01.025.h4: 2) The Harmony of Justice and Mercy
01.026.p: Divine justice is moderated by wisdom that fully understands weakness [2:3.2], and eternal justice and divine mercy together produce what humans experience as fairness [2:4.4].
01.027.h3: 6. Eternal Fellowship with the Universal Father
01.029.p: The Universal Father bridged the gulf between deity and humanity by sending his spirit to dwell within us [5:1.12], healing the spiritual separation between mortal and divine [2:1.8].
01.031.p: When we choose to do his will, the growth of the immortal soul begins, and eternal survival becomes assured [5:1.11], 5:5.14.
01.033.p: God has joined humanity in an eternal adventure. He lovingly leads to Paradise all children who seek to know him and become like him [5:1.12].
02.title: The Eternal Son
02.001.h3: 1. The Existence and Nature of the Eternal Son
02.002.h4: 1) The mystery of eternity and a beginningless being
02.003.p: In the vast universe of universes, the Eternal Son exists as the complete and final expression of all personal and absolute concepts [6:0.1]. We speak of him as the “first thought” of the Universal Father because of the limitations of human language [6:0.2], yet this is merely a concession to time-bound mortal minds attempting to grasp an eternal reality [6:0.2]. Just as the Father has no beginning, the Eternal Son has no beginning either, and their eternal simultaneity remains a mystery far beyond the comprehension of time-bound creatures [6:0.4].
02.004.h4: 2) The Son as the personalized expression of the Father’s infinite concept
02.005.p: The Eternal Son is a divine reality and an unlimited spirit; he is the personalized expression of the Universal Father’s universal and infinite concept [6:0.3].
02.006.h3: 2. The Status of the Second Source and Center
02.007.h4: 1) The position and creative authority of the Second Source and Center
02.008.p: The Eternal Son is the Son of God, the second person of Deity, and the coordinate creator of all things [6:1.1]. If the Universal Father is the First Source and Center, then the Eternal Son stands as the great Second Source and Center [6:1.1].
02.009.h4: 2) Creative union and the primordial identity of the “Word”
02.010.p: The Father does not personally function as a creator except in union with or through the Eternal Son [6:1.3]. The biblical statement, “⟦Q 6:1.3⟧In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God… all things were made by him, and without him was not anything made that was made,⟦/Q⟧” was indeed a truthful declaration about the Eternal Son [6:1.3].
02.011.h3: 3. The Personal Nature of the Eternal Son
02.013.p: The Eternal Son is entirely like the Father and is, in fact, the personal revelation of the Universal Father to all creation [6:2.2]. Therefore, the saying “⟦Q 6:2.2⟧He who has seen the Son has seen the Father⟦/Q⟧” is eternally true [6:2.2]. The Son possesses all of the Father’s divine personality and spiritual attributes in full measure [6:2.5].
02.014.h4: 2) The Son’s cooperation in the spiritual ascent of creatures
02.015.p: The Eternal Son shares in the responsibility of assisting all creatures who strive toward spiritual perfection and progress [6:2.4].
02.016.h3: 4. The Mercy of the Eternal Son
02.017.h4: 1) The nature and absoluteness of mercy
02.018.p: The most striking attribute of the Eternal Son is mercy [6:3.1]. As the Father is love, the Son is mercy [6:3.1]. He is the great minister of mercy to all creation, and mercy constitutes the very essence of his spiritual personality [6:3.2].
02.019.h4: 2) The Son’s mercy as the expression of the Father’s love
02.020.p: It is crude and incorrect to imagine that the Eternal Son pleads with the Father to be merciful [6:3.4]. Every merciful ministry performed by the Sons of God is a direct revelation of the Father’s universal love and infinite compassion [6:3.4]. Mercy is simply the Father’s love expressed in action through the personality of the Eternal Son [6:3.5].
02.021.h3: 5. The Spiritual Sovereignty of the Eternal Son
02.022.h4: 1) The absolute control of spiritual gravity
02.023.p: The Eternal Son exercises absolute spiritual sovereignty by controlling and administering all spiritual realities through the spiritual-gravity circuit [7:1.1]. He literally holds all pure spirits and spiritual beings within his grasp [7:1.1]. This spiritual gravity suffers no time delay and is unaffected by space [7:1.2].
02.025.p: While sin and rebellion may disturb the circuits of a local universe, they cannot suspend or hinder the Eternal Son’s absolute spiritual gravity [7:1.7].
02.026.h4: 3) The spiritual drawing power that lifts ascendant souls
02.027.p: The secret of human soul ascension toward Paradise lies in the drawing power of the Eternal Son’s spiritual gravity [7:3.2].
02.029.h4: 1) The indivisibility of the Son and the impossibility of indwelling
02.030.p: The purely personal nature of the Eternal Son cannot be fragmented, and thus he cannot indwell human experience as the Father’s spirit fragments do [7:3.1].
02.031.h4: 2) Bestowal as the method of approaching created beings
02.032.p: The Eternal Son compensates for this limitation through the technique of bestowal [7:5.4]. His Creator Sons approach created personalities by assuming creature nature and incarnating in the likeness of their own creation [7:5.4]. As we know the Father through the Creator Son of Nebadon who incarnated on Urantia [7:7.6], so one who has seen these Paradise Sons has, in a true and spiritual sense, seen the Eternal Son [7:7.3].
02.033.h3: 7. The Son as the Exclusive Revealer of the Father
02.034.h4: 1) The unique and complete revelation of the Father
02.035.p: The Eternal Son is the complete and exclusive personal revelation of the Father’s spirit and personality [7:7.1]. His divine Sons likewise reveal the way by which created beings may come to the Father [7:7.4]. In nature of personality and divinity, the Father and the Son are coordinate and equal [7:7.1].
02.036.h4: 2) The eventual face-to-face meeting in Paradise
02.037.p: As ascending beings progress spiritually and draw nearer to Paradise, the personality of the Eternal Son becomes increasingly real to them [6:8.5]. At last, in the fullness of eternity, they will stand in the presence of his majestic and glorious being [6:8.8].
03.title: The Infinite Spirit
03.001.h3: 1. The Eternal Emergence of the Infinite Spirit
03.002.h4: 1) The united will of the Father and the Son giving rise to the Infinite Spirit
03.003.p: In the dawn of eternity, when the infinite and absolute thought of the Universal Father found its divine expression in the Eternal Son, these two—Thought-God and Word-God—longed for a universal and limitless agent who could execute their united action [8:0.1]. At this eternal moment, the Father and the Son became infinitely self-aware of their absolute union, and throughout the cycles of eternity they entered into a divine partnership to bring their unified concept into action [8:0.2]. It is precisely at this moment that the Third Person of Deity, the Infinite Spirit, emerges in full personal reality [8:0.3].
03.004.h4: 2) The apparent sequence of origin and the eternal coexistence of the Three Persons
03.005.p: Although a sequence appears in the origin of the Infinite Spirit, this is only for the purpose of enabling finite minds to comprehend their relationship [8:0.4]. In truth, all three—Father, Son, and Spirit—have existed eternally [8:0.4], equal, absolute, and forever united in personality [8:0.4].
03.006.h3: 2. The Spirit as the God of Action
03.007.h4: 1) The executive of the Father’s purpose through the Son
03.008.p: The Infinite Spirit is the God of Action; when the Paradise Trinity came into existence, he became the executive agent who fulfills the Father’s purpose through the personality of the Eternal Son [8:1.1], 8:1.3.
03.009.h4: 2) The awakening of space and the birth of Havona
03.010.p: When the Infinite Spirit functions, the quiescent reservoirs of space stir, and a billion perfect spheres come into existence [8:1.4]. At this point, physical gravity and spiritual gravity become distinctly manifest [8:1.4], 8:1.5, and the Infinite Spirit becomes the universe integrator with the unique capacity to unify all levels of reality [9:0.4]. Submissive to the unified will and combined concept of the Father and the Son [8:1.7], he becomes eternal with the birth of the central universe of Havona [8:1.7]. He testifies that when he attained personal consciousness, the central universe simultaneously became eternal [8:1.8].
03.011.h3: 3. Names, Nature, and Attributes of the Infinite Spirit
03.012.h4: 1) The many designations of the Third Source and Center
03.013.p: The Third Source and Center is known by many names: the Universe Spirit, the Supreme Guide, the Divine Actor, the Infinite Mind, the Paradise Mother Spirit, and the Omnipresent Spirit [9:1.1].
03.015.p: His most outstanding attribute is omnipresence [9:1.5]. He fully and without limitation shares the omnipresence of both the Father and the Son [9:1.5]. He fills all organized space, and the presence of the Paradise Deities draws all things and beings inward toward the Paradise center [8:1.6].
03.016.h3: 4. The Ministry of the Infinite Spirit
03.017.h4: 1) The Infinite Spirit as the representative of service
03.018.p: If the Father represents love and the Son represents mercy, the Spirit represents service [8:4.2]. The Infinite Spirit tends to follow the merciful nature of the Eternal Son [8:2.6] and assumes responsibility for the ministry of mercy [8:2.6]. Mercy is the eternal unification of the Father’s love and the Son’s compassion applied to the creation of creatures [8:4.2], forming the foundation of universal ministry [8:4.2].
03.019.h4: 2) The Spirit as the unceasing minister to mind
03.020.p: The core of the Infinite Spirit’s ministry is his constant service to mind [8:4.1]. As the Absolute Mind [ 9:1.1], he is the source of mind endowment throughout the universes [9:1.1], the center of mind, and the universal administrator of all mental realms [9:1.5]. The domain of creature mind has an exclusive origin in the Third Source and Center, and even Thought Adjusters cannot indwell the human mind until the Infinite Spirit prepares the mind for their spiritual function [9:5.2].
03.021.h3: 5. The Spirit’s Role in Guiding Ascenders
03.022.h4: 1) The Spirit as the effective guide of truth-loving souls
03.023.p: The Infinite Spirit is the effective agent who guides all truth-loving souls of all worlds of time and space to the Father and the Son [8:3.5]. Only through the persistent ministry of the Spirit can ascending beings discover the Son [8:3.7], and ascending pilgrims first reach the Infinite Spirit among the Paradise Deities at the center of all things [8:3.8].
03.024.h3: 6. The Infinite Spirit as a True Divine Personality
03.025.h4: 1) The Spirit’s full possession of personal attributes
03.026.p: The Infinite Spirit is not mere force or influence; he is a true divine personality [8:6.1]. He possesses all attributes associated with personality—memory, reasoning, judgment, creative imagination, and will [8:6.3].
03.027.h4: 2) The Spirit’s vast family of ministering beings
03.028.p: His vast family—composed of the Seven Master Spirits, the ministering spirits, and innumerable orders of helpers—devotedly assist all creatures in their upward progress toward higher levels of spiritual attainment [8:4.4].
03.029.h3: 7. The Spirit as the Harmonizer of the Universal Symphony
03.030.h4: 1) The Spirit as the cosmic conductor of divine execution
03.031.p: The ministry of the Infinite Spirit resembles that of a great conductor leading the orchestra of the universe. He takes the Father’s plan (love) and the Son’s melody (mercy) and executes them in such a way that they reach the minds of all creatures, producing universal harmony—the perfect expression of divine service.
04.title: The Trinity
04.001.h3: 1. The Trinity as a Universal Reality
04.002.h4: 1) The inseparable union of three divine persons underlying all existence and reality
04.003.p: At the foundation of all existence and reality lies the inseparable union of three divine persons—the Trinity [8:1.3]. The Urantia Book unfolds this divine union not merely as a religious doctrine but as a vast and exquisitely organized cosmic reality. The traditional human concept of the Trinity, held for thousands of years, expands into a three-level union: the Paradise Trinity, the Ultimate Trinity, and the Absolute Trinity [106:6.2]. Many of the confusions found in traditional Christian theology arose from failing to distinguish the persons of the Paradise Trinity from the creators and administrators of the local universes [4:5.2].
04.004.h3: 2. The Nature of the Paradise Trinity
04.005.h4: 1) The eternal and absolute union of the Father, Son, and Spirit
04.006.p: The central nucleus of The Urantia Book is the Paradise Trinity, the eternal and absolute union of the Universal Father (First Source and Center), the Eternal Son (Second Source and Center), and the Infinite Spirit (Third Source and Center, the Conjoint Actor) [8:0.3], 8:1.3. These three are equal, absolute, and eternally united persons [8:0.4], yet their functions are distinctly differentiated in the cosmic hierarchy.
04.007.h4: 2) A fundamental difference from traditional Christianity—the distinction between the Eternal Son and Jesus
04.008.p: Unlike traditional Christianity, the Eternal Son is not identified with Jesus Christ. The Jesus regarded as “God the Son” in Christian theology is, in fact, one of the many Creator Sons of the Eternal Son—a Michael Son—who incarnated on Urantia as his bestowal [21:1.1], 21:3.24. The Eternal Son is the absolute personality who perfectly expresses the Father’s infinite thought [6:0.1], 6:7.1, and he is the original source from whom all Creator Sons inherit their creative divinity. The Creator Son Michael is the divine and perfect likeness of the Eternal Son [7:5.11], 6:2.2, and Jesus is the revelation of this Michael Son in human form [1:6.3], 1:6.8, 3:6.7.
04.009.h4: 3) The distinction between the Infinite Spirit and the Holy Spirit—the difference between the Source and the local expression
04.010.p: The Infinite Spirit is not the Holy Spirit, but the source of the Holy Spirit. In The Urantia Book, the Infinite Spirit is the God of Action—the executor of the united will of the Father and the Son—and the origin of absolute mind [9:1.1], 9:5.2. In contrast, the being referred to in Christianity as the “Holy Spirit” is actually the spiritual circuit of the Creative Spirit, the local universe representative of the Infinite Spirit [8:5.3]. The Infinite Spirit is the omnipresent spiritual influence—the Everywhere-present Spirit [8:5.1]—while the Holy Spirit is a limited spiritual circuit operating only within a given local universe [8:5.3]. The Creative Spirit, also called the Mother Spirit of a local universe, is the close associate of the Creator Son [9:8.4], and her spiritual ministry to mortals is what Christianity recognizes as the work of the “Holy Spirit” [9:2.5].
04.011.h3: 3. The Cosmic Structure and Authority of the Trinity
04.012.h4: 1) A cosmic framework that systematically distinguishes the functions of Deity
04.013.p: The Urantia Book provides a cosmic framework that clearly differentiates the personal identities and functional roles of the Trinity within a complex and hierarchical universe [4:5.2]. The Paradise Trinity creates the central universe, holds all creation together through its control and gravity, and delegates authority to subordinate divine personalities such as the Creator Sons [10:3.17], 10:3.10.
04.014.h3: 4. The Two Experiential Extensions of the Trinity
04.015.h4: 1) The Ultimate Trinity—union with the Supreme Being
04.016.p: The first experiential extension of the Paradise Trinity is the Ultimate Trinity, which represents the union of the Paradise Trinity with the Supreme Being, who is progressively becoming personalized through the evolutionary experiences of finite creatures [10:7.3]. The Supreme Being is not yet complete in the unification of power and personality [10:7.3], 10:7.4, and this evolving Deity is the finite reflection of the Paradise Trinity [14:6.23]. The Supreme Being is the closest comprehensible concentration of Trinity power-personality available to finite creatures [10:5.4].
04.017.h4: 2) The Absolute Trinity—union with the Absolutes
04.018.p: The second expansion, the Absolute Trinity, is implied to arise when the Paradise Trinity unites with the Universal Absolute, the Deity Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute [4:1.8]. The mysterious cooperative action of these Absolutes produces unpredictable cosmic reactions that can dissolve matter, transcend mind, and reveal spirit. This domain extends beyond the present universe age and includes the unorganized and uninhabited outer space levels [12:3.8], 12:3.10.
04.019.h3: 5. The Urantia Book’s Advanced Cosmology of the Trinity
04.020.h4: 1) The multi-level structure of existential, experiential, and transcendental Deity
04.021.p: The Urantia Book enlarges the Trinity into three dimensions:
04.022.p: Existential Deity – the eternal Paradise Trinity
04.023.p: Experiential Deity – the Ultimate Trinity and the Supreme Being
04.025.p: Thus providing an advanced cosmology that surpasses the limitations of traditional Christian theology in distinguishing the identity and function of Deity [4:5.2].
04.026.h3: 6. A New Illustrative Perspective for Understanding the Trinity
04.027.h4: 1) Understanding the Trinity as the structure of a cosmic government
04.028.p: All of this may be understood by analogy to a national governing system. Traditional Christianity focuses on the three persons of the central government (Father, Son, and Spirit), while The Urantia Book explains how this central government (the Paradise Trinity) creates and administers local governments (the Creator Sons and the Creative Spirits), and how the experiences of these local governments contribute to the future development and destiny of the whole universe (the Ultimate Trinity and the Absolute Trinity). It is, in effect, a detailed organizational blueprint of universal administration.
05.title: The Differentiation of the I AM and the Relationship of Deities
05.001.h3: 1. The Differentiation Originating from the Absolute Nature of the Universal Father
05.002.h4: 1) The infinite and self-existent First Source and Center
05.003.p: The Universal Father, the First Source and Center, is the origin and foundation of all things and beings. He is eternal and infinite [2:1.2] and exists by his own inherent nature [4:4.1]. Because he possesses an infinite nature [2:1.3], all potentials of divinity are inherent within his absoluteness [10:8.4]. As this infinite God differentiates and organizes himself through his creative will, a magnificent union and hierarchy of divine beings emerges, sustaining and governing the vast universes.
05.004.h3: 2. The Paradise Trinity: The Completion of Existential Deity
05.005.h4: 1) The triune personalization of Father, Son, and Spirit
05.006.p: The first and most fundamental differentiation of the Universal Father is the completion of the Paradise Trinity [8:1.3]. At the dawn of eternity, the Father’s infinite thought is personalized as the Eternal Son [6:0.3]. This Thought-God and this Word-God, recognizing their absolute and eternal oneness [8:0.2], give rise to the Infinite Spirit who executes their united action [8:0.3].
05.007.h4: 2) The triune cycle and the existential personalization of Deity
05.008.p: The completion of this triune cycle expresses the divine will of self-bestowal and personality-sharing inherent in the Father’s free will [10:1.3]. The Father bestows his personality upon the Eternal Son [10:1.4], and together they bring into existence the conjoint personality of the Infinite Spirit, thus completing the existential personalization of Deity [10:2.2]. In this manner, the Father, the Son, and the Spirit become unique, original, and unified persons [10:2.6], and collectively they form the minimum necessary reality to contain all potentials of divinity [10:8.4].
05.009.h3: 3. God the Sevenfold: The Realization of Deity in Time and Space
05.010.h4: 1) From existential Trinity to experiential Deity
05.011.p: While the Paradise Trinity is absolute and existential, the hierarchy of divine beings who actually administer the universes of time and space and who contact evolutionary creatures is revealed as the Deity of Sevenfold [3:1.12]. This system functions as the Paradise Trinity unites with the evolutionary and experiential Deity of the universes, the Supreme Being [9:1.6].
05.012.h4: 2) The components and roles of the Sevenfold Deity
05.013.p: The primary personalities and functions constituting the Sevenfold Deity are as follows.
05.014.p: The Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit [8:1.3].
05.015.p: The Seven Master Spirits: the first divine acts of the Infinite Spirit functioning apart from the Trinity [9:8.2], distributing the Infinite Spirit to each superuniverse [16:2.4].
05.016.p: The Paradise Creator Sons: the Sons created jointly by the Father and the Eternal Son, who rule sovereignly within each local universe.
05.017.p: The Ancients of Days: direct creations of the Paradise Trinity, administering the seven superuniverses and executing judicial judgment [15:2.8], 2:3.3.
05.018.p: The Supreme Being: the experiential unifying Deity of the finite universes [10:7.4].
05.019.h3: 4. The Rise of the Supreme Being and His Relation to Finite Creatures
05.020.h4: 1) An experiential Deity who becomes personalized through finite experience
05.021.p: At the center of the Sevenfold Deity stands the evolving Supreme Being. This Deity becomes personalized and empowered through the experience, progress, and achievements of the universe creatures [10:7.4]. He is the beginning of the power-personality synthesis of the finite reflection of the Paradise Deities [1:5.13] and is connected to the central presence of the Paradise Father, where all lines of universal gravity converge [11:1.4].
05.022.h4: 2) The Father’s sharing of finite experience and the progressive ascent toward the Supreme
05.023.p: Finite creatures are indispensable to the evolution of the Supreme Being. Although the Universal Father does not gain experience in the way finite creatures imagine [1:5.14], he nonetheless participates in the imperfect experience-consciousness of all striving beings [2:2.6]. The progressive experience of finite creatures becomes part of the Father’s endlessly expanding divine self-realization within the sacred cycle of growth. Ascending mortals reach the Supreme Being in Havona [14:6.38], and their spiritual advancement ultimately ends the isolation between the superuniverses when the personal sovereignty of the Supreme becomes fully factualized [3:1.10]. The Supreme Being is the closest concentration of Trinity power-personality comprehensible to finite creatures [10:5.4], and for this reason the Trinity as related to finite beings is sometimes called the Trinity of Supremacy [10:5.4].
05.024.h3: 5. The Transcendent Expansion of Deity: The Ultimate and the Absolute
05.025.h4: 1) The Ultimate Trinity and the Ultimate Deity
05.026.p: The functions of the Trinity extend beyond the existential level and reach into the realms of the Ultimate and the Absolute. The Paradise Trinity relates to realities that are above the finite but below the absolute, a level known as the Trinity of Ultimacy [10:5.5]. The Ultimate Trinity supervises the transcendent evolution and integration of the master universe. In the present universe age, the Paradise Trinity appears to sustain a relationship with the Ultimate Deity analogous to its cooperation with the incomplete power-personality of the Supreme Being [10:7.3]. The Ultimate will be revealed, or is destined to be revealed, on the outer edges of the fourth universe level of space [12:6.13].
05.027.h4: 2) The Absolute Trinity and the mystery of Absolute Deity
05.028.p: The highest unification of Deity is the Absolute Trinity. The Urantia Book refers to the Deity Absolute [10:8.5], the Universal Absolute [12:6.13], and the Unqualified Absolute [4:1.8]. The mysterious coordination of these three Absolutes produces unpredictable cosmic reactions that dissolve matter, transcend mind, and reveal spirit, a phenomenon that continually perplexes the observer [4:1.8]. The Deity Absolute may be universally existent but cannot be said to be present in space [12:6.13]. The Paradise Trinity is implied to unite with these three Absolutes to form the Absolute Trinity.
05.030.h4: 1) Direct creations of the Paradise Trinity
05.031.p: The Paradise Trinity directly creates exalted subordinate personalities who constitute the administrative structure of the universes [10:2.8]. These are known as Trinity-origin personalities, dedicated to the judicial and administrative affairs of the superuniverses. Representative examples include the following.
05.032.p: A. The Ancients of Days: rulers of the superuniverses [18:3.8].
05.033.p: B. The Perfectors of Wisdom: beings who unite Paradise wisdom with evolutionary experiential insight, capable of participating in all celestial service for ascending mortals [19:2.6].
05.034.p: C. The Perfections of Days: 210 personalities presiding over the major sectors of each superuniverse [18:4.1].
05.035.p: D. The Unions of Days: ambassadors of the Paradise Trinity to the constellation headquarters of each local universe [15:2.4].
05.036.p: E. The Trinity Teacher Sons: superb instructors spread throughout the grand universe, serving all human and divine personalities [7:6.6].
05.037.h3: 7. The Universal Harmony Achieved Through the Father’s Differentiation
05.038.h4: 1) Differentiation does not diminish divinity but enables creation to experience it
05.039.p: The differentiation of the self-existing Universal Father does not diminish his infinite nature in the slightest [3:4.1]. Instead, it establishes a magnificent hierarchy through which his love and perfection can be experienced and recognized in countless ways across all creation [ 2:2.5].
06.title: The Divine Central Universe
06.001.h3: 1. Paradise: The Eternal Center Where Divinity and Reality Meet
06.002.h4: 1) Paradise as the sacred dwelling place of the Gods
06.003.p: At the eternal center of all creation lies Paradise, the divine abode of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, and their sacred associates [11:0.1]. This central Isle is not only the most massively organized material structure in all existence [11:0.1] but also functions as the spiritual dwelling of Deity [17:0.1]. Paradise has existed from eternity, and no record or legend speaks of its origin—it is the abiding nucleus of light and life [11:0.2].
06.004.h4: 2) Material stability and the function of absolute centrality
06.005.p: Since all the Father’s intellectual creation is based upon material habitation, the center of absolute control—Paradise—is likewise a literal material reality [11:0.1]. Paradise consists of absolutum, a unique form of nonliving yet nondead primordial substance [11:2.9], a solitary, unrepeated entity in all the universes [11:2.9]. Space appears to originate just beneath lower Paradise, and time seems to spring forth from upper Paradise [11:2.11].
06.006.h3: 2. The Form and Structural Nature of Paradise
06.008.p: Paradise differs completely in form from inhabited space bodies [11:2.2]. It is not spherical but elliptical, with the north–south diameter one-sixth longer than the east–west diameter [11:2.2]. The vertical thickness from upper to lower surface is only one-tenth of the east–west diameter, rendering Paradise essentially flat [11:2.2].
06.009.h4: 2) The three functional zones of the central Isle
06.010.p: The central Isle is divided into three functional regions: upper Paradise, peripheral Paradise, and lower Paradise [11:2.4]–2.7. Upper Paradise is the realm of personal activity, while the periphery serves nonpersonal and nonspiritual functions [11:2.8]. Lower Paradise contains the mysterious domain from which space seems to flow outward [11:2.11].
06.011.h3: 3. Paradise as the Absolute Center of Universal Function
06.012.h4: 1) The Father’s immovable position at the universe’s center
06.013.p: The Universal Father is always found at this central location on Paradise [11:1.4]. Were he to move from his position, the universe would plunge into chaos, for all lines of gravity converge into him from the farthest reaches of creation [11:1.4]. His fixed position serves as the absolute axis of stability for all universes.
06.014.h4: 2) The nature and uniqueness of Paradise substance
06.015.p: Paradise consists of absolutum, a fixed and unique form of matter [11:2.9] that is neither alive nor lifeless. This primordial substance is the Father’s first nonspiritual expression and cannot be duplicated anywhere in creation [11:2.9]. Paradise stands alone as the solitary source-form reality of the master universe.
06.016.h3: 4. The Perfect Central Universe Surrounding Paradise: Havona
06.017.h4: 1) The structure and character of the eternal Havona creation
06.018.p: Surrounding Paradise is Havona, the central universe. Havona is an eternal creation [12:1.10], composed of one billion perfect worlds [14:3.4], 15:2.9. No two of these worlds are alike; each is uniquely designed and flawlessly executed [14:5.6]. The Havona spheres are arranged in seven concentric circuits, and in the innermost regions the Father’s seven secret spheres transmit the most intense spiritual luminosity to the circuits [13:0.3].
06.019.h4: 2) Havona as the purpose-filled reflection of divine perfection
06.020.p: Havona is the perfect archetype of divinity, designated by the Universal Father as the eternal force-center of all expanding universes of time and space [14:6.10]. It serves as the ideal pattern inspiring the Creator Sons to perfect their local universes [14:6.27] and functions as the training ground where they receive essential preparation [14:6.27]. The native Havona residents embody the divine will by their very nature [14:4.13].
06.021.h3: 5. The Ascent of Mortal Travelers Through Havona Toward Paradise
06.022.h4: 1) The ascent through the seven circuits of Havona
06.023.p: A mortal ascending from evolutionary worlds arrives first at the outermost reception world of the seventh circuit [14:3.4]. From this point, the pilgrim proceeds inward, world by world and circuit by circuit, undergoing final tests that qualify them to reach Deity [14:3.4]. In this ascent the pilgrim encounters the pre-Paradise Deity, the Supreme Being [14:6.38].
06.024.h4: 2) The understanding gained in Havona as the passport to Paradise
06.025.p: The most essential attainment of the pilgrim in Havona is understanding, which becomes the passport allowing entrance to Paradise [26:4.15]. The educational system of the central universe prepares the ascending mortal to stand in the presence of the Gods.
06.026.h3: 6. The Cooperative Functions of the Trinity Within the Central Universe
06.027.h4: 1) The operational centers of the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit
06.028.p: The activities of the Paradise Trinity are profoundly linked to the central universe. The Eternal Son uses Havona as the headquarters of his spiritual gravity control [14:6.14], while the Infinite Spirit performed earlier phases of his ministry within this perfect creation before serving in the evolutionary universes [14:6.18].
06.029.h4: 2) The arena of the Sevenfold Deity and the fulfillment of divine ideals
06.030.p: Havona is the arena where the coordinated actions of the Sevenfold Deity unfold [15:0.1]. It is also the dwelling where the perfect ideals of divine beauty and truth are fully realized [14:6.11]. In the central universe, the hope of all ascending creatures finds its ultimate fulfillment.
06.031.h3: 7. The Future Destiny After Reaching Paradise
06.032.h4: 1) The Corps of the Finality and the missions of future universes
06.033.p: Upon attaining residence on Paradise, a mortal begins the progressive realization of divinity and transcendence [30:4.31]. Such perfected beings are assembled into the Corps of the Finality, whose future mission is believed to relate to the universes now forming in outer space [31:0.8].
06.034.h4: 2) The eternal role of Havona as the divine archetype
06.035.p: Havona will remain forever the eternal pattern of perfect beauty and truth for all creation [11:9.6], an unchanging exemplar of divine reality for both present and future universes.
07.title: The Seven Superuniverses
07.001.h3: 1. The Origin of the Seven Superuniverses and the Formation of the Grand Universe
07.002.h4: 1) The emergence of the seven superuniverses after the creation of Havona
07.003.p: After the Paradise Trinity—composed of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit—brought the eternal and perfect central universe Havona into existence, the vast space surrounding this flawless creation became the setting for the evolutionary realms known as the seven superuniverses [12:1.5]. Together, these seven superuniverses and Havona constitute the Grand Universe, the totality of the presently organized and inhabited creation [12:1.13].
07.004.h4: 2) The unfinished condition of the present Grand Universe
07.005.p: The seven superuniverses are still incomplete, and the outer rim of the Grand Universe remains irregular and unfinished [12:1.13]. Excluding the one billion worlds of the central creation, the Grand Universe contains the evolutionary potential of more than seven trillion inhabitable worlds [12:1.13], 15:2.1, though this does not include architectural headquarters spheres. Your local universe, Nebadon, belongs to the seventh superuniverse, Orvonton [12:1.12], a creation illuminated and warmed by more than ten trillion suns [15:6.10].
07.006.h3: 2. The Position and Spatial Arrangement of the Seven Superuniverses
07.007.h4: 1) The great elliptical orbit around the central universe
07.008.p: The seven superuniverses are arranged in a vast elliptical orbit around Havona, traveling at the first space level of the master universe structure [12:1.3], 12:1.5. They rotate in a counterclockwise direction. This arrangement is not a rigid physical organization but a geographical grouping of one-seventh of post-Havona creation.
07.009.h4: 2) Structural symmetry and comparative scale of each superuniverse
07.010.p: Each superuniverse is approximately equal in the number of local universes it contains and the space it occupies [12:1.12]. This balanced design reveals the ordered purpose behind the sevenfold division and maintains a unified cosmic structure.
07.011.h3: 3. The Administrative Structure and Divine Rulers of the Superuniverses
07.013.p: The seven superuniverses function through a carefully ordered administrative hierarchy designed to guide ascending beings from the farthest worlds toward Paradise [14:5.4]. Each administrative level has an architectural sphere as its headquarters, governed by divine personalities.
07.014.p: Below is a summary of the order, population, headquarters, and principal rulers:
07.016.p: Composed of about 1,000 inhabited worlds, administered from an architectural sphere such as Jerusem. Ruled by a System Sovereign [15:2.3].
07.018.p: Made of 100 systems (about 100,000 worlds). Headquarters is an architectural world such as Edentia. Represented by a Union of Days, an ambassador of the Paradise Trinity [18:7.1].
07.020.p: Contains 100 constellations (about 10,000,000 worlds). The capital is Salvington, ruled by a Creator Son [21:2.1].
07.022.p: Composed of 100 local universes (about 1,000,000,000 worlds). Headquarters is the Third Minor Sector, ruled by three Recently Perfected of Days [18:5.1], 15:2.6.
07.024.p: Made of 100 minor sectors (about 100,000,000,000 worlds). Headquarters is the Fifth Major Sector, ruled by three Perfections of Days [18:4.1], 15:2.7.
07.026.p: Composed of 10 major sectors (about 1,000,000,000,000 worlds). Its capital is Uversa, ruled by three Ancients of Days [15:2.8].
07.027.h4: 2) The judicial and executive authority of the Ancients of Days
07.028.p: The superuniverses are governed by three Ancients of Days [15:10.3]. They are Trinity-origin beings, the most perfect and divinely endowed rulers in time and space [18:3.8], incapable of failure or rebellion. Though existentially perfect, they do not possess experiential sovereignty, which someday will be assumed by the experiential God, the Supreme Being [18:3.8].
07.029.h3: 4. Functions of the Superuniverses and Their Divine Administration
07.030.h4: 1) The unifying influence of the Seven Master Spirits
07.031.p: The seven superuniverses are coordinated by the Seven Master Spirits, the diversified and complete expression of the Infinite Spirit’s supreme-ultimate nature [16:4.1], 16:2.4. Each Master Spirit distributes the Infinite Spirit’s attributes across its assigned superuniverse and collaborates with the Seven Supreme Executors on the special worlds of the Infinite Spirit [15:10.1].
07.032.h4: 2) The judicial system: wisdom, counsel, and censure
07.033.p: On Uversa dwell the Perfectors of Wisdom, the Divine Counselors, and the Universal Censors [15:10.5]–10.7. These Trinity-origin beings comprise the judicial administration of the superuniverses [19:3.4].
07.034.p: The Universal Censor synthesizes the insights of the “One Who Is and Was” (Perfectors of Wisdom) and the “One Who Will Be” (Divine Counselors), producing a unified Trinity judgment [19:4.4].
07.035.p: Uversa is also the headquarters for the Reflective Spirits [15:10.2], who reproduce every phase of Paradise Deity with flawless precision and form the communication network between central and local universes [17:3.1].
07.036.h3: 5. Uversa: Capital of the Seventh Superuniverse, Orvonton
07.037.h4: 1) Uversa’s governmental structure and harmony of authority
07.038.p: Uversa, the capital of Orvonton, is the spiritual and administrative center of roughly one trillion worlds [15:7.11]. Its government blends the flawless executive authority of the Ancients of Days with a legislative assembly composed of evolutionary representatives from the inhabited realms [15:11.1]. Remarkably, these two branches have never disagreed and have always worked in perfect harmony [15:11.3].
07.039.h4: 2) Ascending training and the time system of Uversa
07.040.p: Uversa is encircled by seven educational spheres where ascending mortals undergo advanced training before proceeding toward Havona. A standard superuniverse day equals nearly 30 Urantia days, and a Uversa year equals exactly 3,000 Urantia days minus 22 minutes [15:7.2].
07.041.h3: 6. Energy Regulation and the Future Creation Beyond the Superuniverses
07.042.h4: 1) The Universe Power Directors and the cosmic respiration cycle
07.043.p: While orbiting the central universe, the superuniverses participate in the 2-billion-year cycle of cosmic respiration, expanding and contracting in rhythmic phases [12:4.12]. The Universe Power Directors regulate these energies [29:0.4], controlling thirty distinct phases of force and energy [29:4.20]. These directors are semi-material offspring of the Seven Master Spirits [29:1.1].
07.044.h4: 2) The outer space levels and the uncreated future universes
07.045.p: Beyond the seven superuniverses lie the vast outer space levels [12:1.6], the regions destined for future creation and the potential domain of the Ultimate [12:6.13]. Uversa physicists estimate that the presently organized universes utilize only about 5 percent of Paradise’s absolute gravity, while the remaining 95 percent acts upon the unorganized mass realms beyond the Grand Universe [12:3.8]. These domains are the stage for the future evolutionary ages [12:2.4].
07.046.h3: 7. The Purpose of the Superuniverses and the Ascenders’ Path to Perfection
07.047.h4: 1) The educational, judicial, and administrative purpose of the superuniverses
07.048.p: The superuniverses function as divine administrative and educational structures designed to prepare ascending mortals for the long journey inward toward Paradise [1:0.4]. Here, evolutionary beings learn to harmonize justice, mercy, and righteousness as they progress through the divine hierarchy.
07.049.h4: 2) The path toward perfection for all ascending mortals
07.050.p: The Universal Father’s command, “⟦Q 1:0.3⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect⟦/Q⟧” [1:0.3], sets the tone for the ascent of all evolutionary beings. The seven superuniverses constitute the living schools in which mortals grow, are tested, and gradually become worthy of entering Havona and eventually Paradise.
08.title: The Seven Master Spirits
08.001.h3: 1. The Origin and Nature of the Seven Master Spirits
08.002.h4: 1) Their emergence as the first creative act of the Infinite Spirit
08.003.p: The Seven Master Spirits are the direct result of the creative activity of the Infinite Spirit, appearing as the very first creative act performed by the Third Source and Center as Deity [16:0.1]. They are the active and unified representation of the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, standing as the eternal portrait of the Sevenfold God in time and space [8:0.3]. Their existence also reveals the remarkable power of the Conjoint Actor in completing the liberation of the Universal Father from the centralized constraints of perfection and personality absolutism [8:0.3]. They began their ministry simultaneously with the formation of the seven superuniverses [9:8.2].
08.004.h4: 2) Their status as essential components of the Sevenfold God
08.005.p: The Seven Master Spirits constitute the sevenfold personalization of Deity functioning in time and space and within the seven superuniverses, forming a central component of the Sevenfold God. They are eternally fixed as everlasting administrators of the grand universe [0:8.11]. Because they personalize physical energy, cosmic mind, and the spiritual presence of the triune Deity, the statement “the seven spirits of God sent forth into all the universe” is literally true [16:4.1].
08.006.h4: 3) Their abodes and sphere of influence
08.007.p: The dwelling places of the Seven Master Spirits are the Seven Worlds of the Infinite Spirit, from which they govern the destinies of the seven superuniverses and broadcast the spiritual radiance of the Third Person of Deity to all creatures of time and space [13:0.5]. Each Master Spirit maintains a rotating force focal point around Paradise, positioned opposite the superuniverse they supervise [16:0.12].
08.008.h3: 2. The Roles and Functions of the Seven Master Spirits
08.009.h4: 1) The primary channel through which the Infinite Spirit operates in the universes
08.010.p: The Seven Master Spirits distribute the Infinite Spirit’s influence throughout creation. They are the sevenfold source of cosmic mind and the full reservoir of intellectual potential for the grand universe [16:6.1]. Cosmic mind diversifies into seven forms corresponding to the seven superuniverses, with each Master Spirit administering one of these phases in the realm assigned to them [42:10.6].
08.011.h4: 2) Their collective representation of the Paradise Trinity
08.012.p: When the Seven Master Spirits assemble within the triune presence of the Paradise Deities, they collectively represent the undivided authority, wisdom, and power of the Trinity to the evolutionary universes [16:1.3]. In this unified state, they encompass all attributes and attitudes of Deity existing on the supreme–ultimate level, manifesting the functional presence of the Trinity throughout the master universe [16:1.3].
08.013.h4: 3) Their connection to the Reflective Spirits
08.014.p: The Master Spirits operate throughout the superuniverse capitals by means of the Reflective Spirits, who exist precisely to reproduce perfectly all phases of the Paradise Deities and their expressions [17:3.1]. This reflective mechanism provides real-time communication and coordination across the grand universe.
08.015.h4: 4) Their influence upon the Creative Spirits of the local universes
08.016.p: Each Creative Mother Spirit receives her personalized nature through the supervisory jurisdiction of the Master Spirit presiding over her superuniverse [34:1.3].
08.017.p: In the case of Orvonton, Master Spirit Number Seven exercises decisive influence over:
08.018.p: A. The initiation of life by the Life Carriers [16:4.9].
08.019.p: B. The activation of the adjutant mind-spirits distributed by the Creative Mother Spirit [16:4.10].
08.020.p: C. The ministry of the Spirit of the Mother Spirit, known on Urantia as the Holy Spirit [16:4.13].
08.021.p: D. The bestowal of the Spirit of Truth by the Creator Son [16:4.14].
08.022.p: E. The reflective coordination of local and superuniverse communication [16:4.15].
08.023.h3: 3. The Individual Characteristics of the Seven Master Spirits
08.024.h4: 1) Diversity rooted in the seven possible combinations of the Paradise Deities
08.025.p: Each Master Spirit embodies one of the seven fundamental combinations of Father, Son, and Spirit, and this intrinsic diversity determines the differing characters and functions of the seven superuniverses [16:3.1].
08.027.p: The direct representative of the Universal Father, expressing His power, love, and wisdom with exceptional effectiveness [16:3.2]. He speaks for the Father in the council of the Seven Master Spirits [16:3.2].
08.029.p: The flawless revelation of the Eternal Son’s nature and personality, speaking on behalf of the Eternal Son in their assemblies [16:3.4].
08.031.p: Especially resembles the Infinite Spirit and directs the activities of many high spiritual beings of the Third Source and Center; He speaks for the Infinite Spirit [16:3.6].
08.033.p: Embodies the combined nature of the Father and the Son and serves as counselor to ascending creatures who have reached the Infinite Spirit and are about to meet the Father and the Son [16:3.8].
08.035.p: Perfectly combines the attributes of the Father and the Infinite Spirit and advises the power directors, force centers, and physical controllers [16:3.10].
08.037.p: Reveals the united personality of the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit and guides all creative activities in the central universe involving these two Deities [16:3.12].
08.038.h3: 4. The Unique Nature of Master Spirit Number Seven (the Spirit of Orvonton)
08.039.h4: 1) His balanced representation of the Paradise Deities
08.040.p: Master Spirit Number Seven, who presides over Orvonton, uniquely represents all three Paradise Deities equally—Father, Son, and Spirit—making Him the only trinitarian-balanced Master Spirit [16:3.14]. He serves as counselor and guide to all ascending pilgrims who reach the stage of transcendent glory in Havona [16:3.14].
08.041.h4: 2) His relation to the Supreme Being and the Trinity assemblies
08.042.p: His nature reveals the fact that the evolving Supreme Being’s personality and spirit derive from the Paradise Trinity [16:3.15]. Thus, He is the foremost representative of the Supreme to the universes and demonstrates a unique relationship with the emerging Deity of the finite level [16:3.15].
08.043.p: He naturally presides over all assemblies of the Seven Master Spirits and speaks whenever the unified attitude of Father, Son, and Spirit—or the spiritual attitude of the Supreme—must be expressed [16:3.15].
08.044.h4: 3) His compensation for the present inaccessibility of the Supreme Being
08.045.p: During the present universe age, when ascending creatures cannot yet directly contact the Supreme Being, Master Spirit Number Seven functions on their behalf in matters related to the personal aspect of the Supreme [16:3.19]. His administration of Orvonton reveals a perfect blending of the divine qualities of the Father, Son, and Spirit [16:3.20].
09.title: The Ancients of Days
09.001.p: These beings are the supreme administrators and judicial authorities of each superuniverse, occupying one of the most critical stages in the ascension pathway of finite creatures progressing toward Paradise.
09.002.h3: 1. The Identity and Trinity Relationship of the Ancients of Days
09.003.h4: 1) Their place within the Sevenfold Deity
09.004.p: The Ancients of Days are not part of the Paradise Trinity itself, yet they constitute a central element of the Sevenfold God, the functional Deity through whom finite creatures gain progressive access to the presence of the Infinite God [0:8.9]. The Sevenfold God operates within time and space to aid evolutionary creatures until they eventually achieve power-personality synthesis within the Supreme Being [0:8.9].
09.006.p: They cannot be infinite because they consist of derived Deities—realities that emerged through the experiential actualization of beings created by the eternal Paradise Trinity [0:12.3]. Though perfect and divine, they are not existential as the Paradise Deities are.
09.007.h4: 3) Their relation to the Supreme Being
09.008.p: God the Supreme is becoming actualized within the Creator Sons, the Ancients of Days, and the Master Spirits [0:8.10]. The Supreme derives His experiential almighty power, especially within the superuniverses of time and space, through the authority and jurisdiction of the Ancients of Days [0:8.10].
09.009.h4: 4) Their status as fixed and eternal administrators
09.010.p: Unlike Creator Sons and their divine associates, the Ancients of Days and the Master Spirits are eternally fixed as unchanging administrators throughout the grand universe and will never leave their posts [0:8.11]. Their rulership is absolute within the evolutionary realms assigned to them.
09.011.h3: 2. The Primary Functions and Ministry of the Ancients of Days
09.013.p: The Ancients of Days preside as the rulers of the superuniverses [15:10.3]. Their domain is intimately linked with the educational regime of the superuniverses, and within all spheres under their jurisdiction, finite creatures encounter the spiritual guidance and personal influence of the Eternal Son permeating the environment [7:2.4]. Their administrative authority is unchanging and eternally established within the grand universe [0:8.11].
09.014.h4: 2) Their essential place in the ascension path
09.015.p: In the ascension of finite beings toward Paradise, mortals advance from the recognition of the Creator Son’s divinity in the local universe up to the jurisdiction of the Ancients of Days in the superuniverse [0:8.9]. They represent the next stage of divine sovereignty that ascending mortals must pass through.
09.016.h4: 3) Rulership of human kingdoms rather than individual lives
09.017.p: Although they are supreme administrators, the Ancients of Days do not primarily govern the inner life of individuals. They influence the collective realms of human civilization rather than the private mind of a single human being. Their rulership is macrocosmic, not personal or intimate.
09.018.h4: 4) Their administration and the incompleteness of the finite
09.019.p: Their government appears to reflect certain marks of developmental incompleteness—an effect of the finite realm’s imperfect response to the Paradise Trinity as well as the unfinished status of the Supreme Being [10:7.4]. Their rulership thus mirrors both evolutionary growth and divine supervision.
09.020.h3: 3. Their Relationship to Annihilation Judgment and Life Creation
09.021.p: A. Judicial authority in rebellion and annihilation
09.023.p: Following the outbreak of the Lucifer rebellion, Michael petitioned the Ancients of Days for authority to confine all personalities implicated in the revolt, a request that was approved with a single exception [53:9.3].
09.025.p: Once Michael completed His final bestowal and assumed undisputed sovereignty of Nebadon, Lucifer—the arch-deceiver—was immediately detained by the Ancients of Days on Uversa [53:9.2]. He has since been held as a prisoner on the first satellite of the Father’s group among the transitional spheres of Jerusem [53:9.2].
09.027.p: A first hearing regarding Gabriel’s petition for the destruction of the rebels has already taken place. Loyal beings expect that the decree from Uversa will soon be issued as an annihilation execution broadcast announcing the extinction of the imprisoned rebels [53:9.7]. When the sentence is pronounced, the rebels will “⟦Q 53:9.7⟧become as though they had not been⟦/Q⟧” [53:9.7].
09.028.p: B. Their connection to life creation and life implantation
09.030.p: Life Carriers acknowledge that aspects of their life implantation work remain mysterious, and they believe that the Ancients of Days have some role in authorizing or influencing life bestowal on new worlds, though they do not fully understand the nature of this involvement [36:6.7].
09.031.h4: 2) Their place within the Sevenfold God
09.032.p: Because the Ancients of Days operate within the Sevenfold God, the functional Deity of the finite universes, they stand alongside Creator Sons as supreme creators within time and space, though their creative role is indirect and administrative rather than personal [36:6.7].
09.035.p: Many personalities commissioned to reveal truth on Urantia today derive their assignments from the Ancients of Days. For instance, the Divine Counselor who describes the nature and activity of the Infinite Spirit received such an appointment from Them [9:8.26].
09.037.p: Ascending mortals, after progressing through the superuniverse training, eventually reach the constellation capitals such as Edentia, where they first hear the narrative of their long careers from the Faithfuls of Days, one of the Trinity-origin beings associated with their destiny [43:9.1].
09.038.h4: 3) Compensation for the incompleteness of the Supreme Being
09.039.p: Because the Supreme Being is not yet fully actualized in the present universe age [0:7.6], the Ancients of Days provide ascending creatures with the necessary integration of power and personality that compensates for this incompleteness [0:8.11]. They assist finite beings in progressing toward absonite attainment beyond the limitations of space and time [0:8.11].
09.040.p: The Ancients of Days function like the majestic central courthouse and supreme administrative complex of the superuniverses. Though They never move from Their eternal administrative positions [0:8.11], Their decisions—such as judgments of annihilation [53:9.7]—and Their oversight of the Sevenfold God’s ascension framework [0:8.12] determine the eternal destiny of all finite creatures.
10.title: The Descending Sons of God
10.001.p: The Descending Sons of God fall into two major groups depending on whether their origin is in Paradise or in the local universe. All of them serve in administration, judgment, life bestowal, and the spiritual uplift of created beings. They function as divine channels through which higher authority is conveyed to lower realms.
10.003.p: This order originates through direct action of the Paradise Trinity and is existentially perfect and divinely complete.
10.005.p: A Creator Son is personalized at the moment the Universal Father and the Eternal Son unite to conceive a new, unique, and absolute personal idea [7:6.3]. He is potentially equal to the Father and the Son in spiritual nature, divine wisdom, and creative power [7:6.3]. Each Creator Son becomes the sovereign ruler of a local universe and the Father of all inhabited worlds within it [1:5.5]. In order to acquire experiential sovereignty, each must undergo a life of bestowal as a mortal creature [7:4.5]. Because they are not fully limited by the infinite wisdom that restricts the Father’s will, they exercise a broader creative free will [4:4.4].
10.007.p: The Avonals are one of the orders created by the Paradise Trinity [20:1.3]. They serve individual planets of a local universe and act as bestowal sons and judicial administrators [20:2.3]. Their ministry on worlds involves three major missions—judicial, administrative, and bestowal service [20:2.5], 20:2.6, 20:2.7. During a bestowal mission, they may appear in human form and may even be born of an earthly mother on certain worlds [20:2.3], while for judicial missions they appear through a technique of incarnation as full-grown adults [20:4.1].
10.009.p: The Daynals are personalized through the united action of the Father, Son, and Spirit [7:6.6] and serve as supreme teachers to both human and divine personalities throughout the grand universe [7:6.6]. They function as liaison beings between Trinity-origin personalities and dual-origin sons within local universe affairs [19:1.1]. They usually remain on a visited planet for a millennium, presiding over a thousand-year dispensation. They do not incarnate or materialize in visible form to mortal creatures.
10.011.p: These four orders are created or organized by the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit of each local universe and form the descending administrative orders of that universe [35:0.7].
10.013.p: The Melchizedeks are created by the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit [35:1.1] and are known as the emergency sons of the local universe [35:4.2]. They participate in judicial and educational administration and served on Urantia as receivers after the Lucifer rebellion [67:3.10]. In a modified material form, a Melchizedek once mated with a material daughter and helped bring into being the Midwayers [36:4.1], 36:4.2. They also believe themselves to be partially involved in the initiation of life on evolutionary worlds.
10.015.p: The Vorondadeks are the Most Highs who rule the constellations [43:5.2], 43:5.3. They are major administrative personalities within the local universe and serve under the counsel of Trinity-origin beings such as the Faithfuls of Days [18:7.2]. They supervise educational work for ascending pilgrims within constellation training worlds [18:7.2]. Their order forms part of the Trinity administrative system extending from constellations to the superuniverse headquarters [15:13.6].
10.017.p: The Lanondadeks constitute the intermediate administrative order of a local universe and include System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes. The farther they operate from the Creator Son, the greater the danger that they may lose their sense of proportional judgment regarding their own importance [50:1.3]. Lucifer and Caligastia are well-known examples of rebellion arising within this order [53:0.1], 39:4.3. They conduct complex duties at system headquarters and frequently represent system rulers as personal agents [35:9.1].
10.019.p: Life Carriers are created by the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit [36:1.1] and belong to the descending sons of the local universe [35:0.2]. Their primary mission is to implant life upon evolutionary worlds [36:3.1]. They can formulate the physical patterns of life, but the spark of life and mind capacity must come from spirit sources [36:6.3], 36:6.4, 36:6.7. They belong to the functional level of the Sevenfold God assigned to the supreme-creators of time and space, and they likely serve as the sevenfold channels through which the river of life flows into all creation. When human-type free will appears on a world, the Life Carriers must withdraw or pledge to cease influencing the biological evolution of that planet [65:1.8].
11.title: The Supreme Being
11.001.p: The Supreme Being, as presented in The Urantia Book, is the experiential Deity who progressively actualizes within time and space. He emerges through the evolution of finite creatures and universes, serving simultaneously as the goal of mortal ascension and the divine unifier of the grand universe.
11.002.h3: 1. Definition and Nature of the Supreme Being
11.004.p: The Supreme Being is a Deity who evolves and actualizes within time and space; He is not an existential Deity but wholly experiential [0:7.5]; and He did not exist in the eternal past but will be eternal only in the eternal future, being conditioned by time and space [0:9.5].
11.006.p: The Supreme Being is the personal Deity in whom creatures and creators achieve experiential unity within time and space [0:7.9]; He grows and experiences similarly to evolving creatures and attains experiential integration with the divine [0:7.7].
11.007.h4: 3) Fusion of the finite and the infinite
11.008.p: When fully actualized, the Supreme Being represents the eternal fusion of the finite and the infinite [0:7.9]; this fusion is the inseparable union of experiential power and spirit personality [0:7.9].
11.010.p: The supreme level is the first stage of Deity understandable by finite beings, and the maximum Deity reality that finite creatures can comprehend is embodied within the Supreme Being [0:3.20].
11.012.p: The Supreme Being is the summation of all finite reality, the Oversoul of the grand universe [117:1.1], the consciousness of the finite cosmos, and the personalization of the shadow of Deity cast upon the finite worlds by the unfathomable nature of the Universal Father [115:7.3].
11.013.h3: 2. Formation and Actualization of the Supreme Being
11.015.p: The Supreme begins as a potential resident within the Paradise Trinity, acquiring personality and spirit attributes within that Trinity [0:8.10], and this potential becomes realized through experiential universe activity [0:9.4].
11.017.p: The Supreme is now actualizing in the grand universe through the Sevenfold God [0:7.7], 0:8.10, and His power expression emerges through the Creator Sons, the Ancients of Days, and the Master Spirits [0:8.10], forming the functional channels of His manifestation in time and space.
11.019.p: The evolving Almighty Supreme, representing impersonal power, unites with the spirit personality of the Supreme Being into one coordinated power-personality synthesis [0:8.10]; the two aspects ultimately merge as the unified Deity of the Supreme [0:7.7], 0:7.10, establishing Him as a personal and cosmic ruler.
11.021.p: The Supreme evolves as the unifier of all personal reality in time and space throughout the grand universe [0:7.8], harmonizing the disparate elements of finite existence.
11.023.p: The evolution of the Supreme is rooted in both the triunity of actuality (Eternal Son, Infinite Spirit, Paradise Isle) and the triunity of potentiality (Deity Absolute, Unqualified Absolute, Universal Absolute) [115:4.2], 115:6.3, these representing the total interplay of growth throughout the universes [115:4.1].
11.025.p: The union of power and personality is achieved through the ministry of the Conjoint Actor [115:4.7], and the emerging Supreme Mind becomes the center of coordination for the grand universe, integrating the Sevenfold God and all cosmic functions [116:1.3].
11.026.h3: 3. Significance and Cosmic Role of the Supreme Being
11.028.p: The Supreme reveals the divine evolution through which descending creators and ascending creatures gain mutual understanding and universal brotherhood [117:1.2], integrating creator causation and creature response within finite experience.
11.029.h4: 2) Dual movement toward Paradise and the Absolutes
11.030.p: He moves inward toward Paradise perfection and outward toward the infinite potential of the Absolutes [115:6.4], a dual motion reflected in all descending and ascending personalities of the universe [115:6.5].
11.032.p: His incompleteness becomes a virtue enabling universe evolution [117:48]; emptiness can be filled through experience [117:2.8]; and the morontia soul grows just as the Supreme grows—through willful and co-creative participation [117:3.7].
11.033.h4: 4) Divine Mother of all evolutionary creatures
11.034.p: The Supreme is the divine Mother of evolving beings [117:6.2], and the morontia soul of mortals is simultaneously the child of the Thought Adjuster (the Father) and the cosmic response of the Supreme (the Mother) [117:6.5].
11.035.h4: 5) Essence of love expressed as brotherhood
11.036.p: The love of the Supreme is the essence of affection expressed in brotherhood [117:6.10], manifesting whenever humans transmit the Father’s love to one another.
11.038.p: The effort of finite beings to reach Paradise perfection creates universe tension which is resolved only within the completed personality of the Supreme Being [116:7.6], the grand integration point of all finite striving.
11.039.h3: 4. Relationship of the Supreme to Other Deities
11.041.p: The Father, Son, and Spirit are existential, whereas the Supreme is wholly experiential [0:7.5]; the experiential Deities—Supreme, Ultimate, and Absolute—are future manifestations derived from the Paradise Trinity [0:9.4]; and the Supreme is the first stage of Trinity unification comprehensible to finite beings [0:9.2].
11.043.p: The Supreme functions through the Paradise personalities of the Sevenfold God, a divine organization that provides the path for finite beings to achieve immortality and be embraced by Infinity [0:8.11].
11.045.p: The Supreme evolves within time and space [0:2.15]; the Ultimate transcends and supersedes these boundaries [0:2.17]; the Absolute expresses the superpersonal meanings and values of Deity [0:2.18]; and all three experiential Deities were latent within the Paradise Trinity [0:12.4].
11.046.h3: 5. Completion, Consequences, and Destiny of the Supreme
11.047.h4: 1) Completion and emergence of the Almighty
11.048.p: The Supreme’s growth will someday culminate in full power-spirit integration [117:2.6]; all finite beings will be liberated from the limitations of incompleteness [117:1.6]; and the completed Supreme will be as personal as the Eternal Son, as substantial as the Paradise Isle, and as unified as the Infinite Spirit.
11.049.h4: 2) Experiential Sovereign of the Grand Universe
11.050.p: When the present universe age is completed, the Supreme will function as the experiential sovereign of the grand universe [117:2.7]; and when His personality and almighty power unify within the Supreme Mind, all universe intelligences will perceive His revealed presence.
11.051.h4: 3) Role in the Trinity of Trinities
11.052.p: He will likely participate as a member of the future Ultimate Trinity [117:7.7], and beyond the grand universe He will engage in superfinite roles in the outer universes [118:10.11] embodying three potentials of hyper-evolutionary manifestation: absonite cooperation, coabsolute relationship, and coinfinite participation [117:7.8]–7.11.
11.054.p: None will personally find the Supreme until the universes reach completed unity and all beings simultaneously discover Him as the perfected Deity of experiential evolution [117:6.21].
12.title: The Creator Sons
12.001.h3: 1. The Origin and Nature of Creator Sons
12.003.p: Creator Sons are beings who create and rule the local universes of time and space [21:0.1], possessing a dual origin that embodies the combined attributes of the Universal Father and the Eternal Son [21:0.1]. When the absolute spiritual concept of the Eternal Son meets the absolute personality concept of the Universal Father, a new Creator Personality instantly emerges [21:1.1]. This being appears endowed with complete divinity, power, and essential nature, lacking none of the qualities of the Infinite Deities [21:1.1].
12.004.h4: 2) Unique Divine Offspring and Archetypal Nature
12.005.p: Every Creator Son is the sole offspring of the perfect union of the original concepts of the two Paradise Parents [21:1.2]. Although their divine nature originates equally from both Parents, some Sons more closely resemble the Father while others resemble the Son [21:1.3]. The administrative character of the Nebadon universe, for example, reflects that its Creator and ruler more closely resembles the Eternal Son in essence and personality [21:1.3]. There are currently more than 700,000 Creator Sons in existence, and no more are being created [21:1.4].
12.007.p: Although Creator Sons share the same origin, they display remarkable diversity in character and creative methods. Each Son reflects his own philosophy of universe administration and unique executive style, which becomes a key factor in shaping the temperament and developmental pattern of his universe. This divine diversity demonstrates the originality of each Son’s personality despite the uniformity of Paradise origin.
12.008.h3: 2. Titles and Universal Roles of Creator Sons
12.009.h4: 1) The Michael Order: Titles and Changes in Status
12.010.p: A Creator Son is originally personalized as a “Michael” [21:0.3]. When he leaves Paradise to begin work in his own universe, he is known as a “Creator Michael,” and after achieving supreme sovereignty, he becomes “Master Michael” [21:0.3]. The Michael order comprehends the entire grand universe [21:0.4] and participates in nearly all types of creature experience, reflecting the breadth of both divine and creature natures [21:0.4].
12.011.h4: 2) Architect, Organizer, and Administrator of the Universe
12.012.p: Creator Sons are the designers, builders, organizers, and supreme administrators of local universes [21:2.1]. Before creating a universe, they undergo long periods of Paradise observation, extensive Havona training, and advanced study of the achievements of other Creator Sons [21:2.1]. Only after completing this preparation do they begin creative operations.
12.013.h4: 3) Companion to Creature Experience and Divine Exemplar
12.014.p: Though a Creator Son does not personally experience every level of creature existence, he profoundly understands and empathizes with the lives of creatures through divine insight and experiential comprehension. His spiritual intuition fully penetrates the growth and struggles of his creatures, making him a living pattern and exemplar for all beings under his jurisdiction.
12.015.h3: 3. Limits of Creative Activity and Relationships with Other Deities
12.016.h4: 1) Cooperation with the Infinite Spirit — The Emergence of the Universe Mother Spirit
12.017.p: A Creator Son must work in close cooperation with the Third Source and Center—the Infinite Spirit—when initiating creative activity [21:2.2]. One Creative Daughter of the Infinite Spirit always accompanies the Creator Son and becomes the Universe Mother Spirit of the new universe [21:2.2]. She functions as co-creator and co-administrator, sharing in the duties of creation, life bestowal, mind ministry, and universe management [21:2.7].
12.018.h4: 2) Creative Limits — Origins of Energy, Life, Personality, and Mind
12.019.p: Although a Creator Son holds vast creative authority, it is not absolute [21:2.3].
12.020.p: Physical energy is governed by the Infinite Spirit; thus, cooperation with the Infinite Spirit is required when introducing new forms of matter [21:2.4].
12.021.p: Life patterns fall under the oversight of the Eternal Son; therefore, his approval is needed for the creation of new life forms [21:2.5].
12.022.p: Personality can be bestowed only by the Universal Father [21:2.6].
12.023.p: Mind is granted by the Third Source and Center to all beings below Paradise Creator level [21:2.7].
12.024.p: For these reasons, a Creator Son operates not independently but within a coordinated Trinity-origin structure.
12.025.h4: 3) Creative Coordination — Joint Creative Action with the Universe Mother Spirit
12.026.p: When a Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit achieve full functional harmony, they initiate the creative union that produces the myriad offspring of the local universe [21:2.9]. This combined creative action is the foundational mechanism responsible for the birth of all subordinate beings in the universe.
12.027.h3: 4. Attainment of Sovereignty and the Seven Bestowals of a Creator Son
12.028.h4: 1) Prerequisite of Sovereignty — Bestowals on Seven Orders of Beings
12.029.p: Although a universe is assigned to a Creator Son, he must complete seven bestowals to achieve supreme experiential sovereignty [21:3.4]. These bestowals involve descending into the seven levels of the creatures he himself created [21:4.2], and must include one incarnation as a mortal of the realm [21:4.3]. This represents the Creator’s voluntary self-humbling to fully experience and understand his creatures’ nature.
12.030.h4: 2) The Final Bestowal on Urantia — Christ Michael
12.031.p: Michael of Nebadon completed six bestowals before performing his seventh and final one on Urantia [21:4.5]. He was born, lived, and died as a human being, and upon the cross proclaimed, “It is finished,” indicating the completion of his bestowal career [21:4.5]. This Urantia bestowal became the decisive experience confirming him as the sovereign Creator and supreme ruler of his universe.
12.032.h4: 3) Exaltation to Sovereignty — King of Kings and Lord of Lords
12.033.p: After completing all bestowals, a Creator Son no longer rules as the representative of the Father but governs by his own earned authority [21:4.5]. He is thereafter known as the King of Kings and Lord of Lords. Michael of Nebadon has exercised this sovereignty for a little over 1,900 years in Urantia’s time [21:3.8].
12.034.h3: 5. The Supreme Sovereignty and Cosmic Destiny of Master Michael
12.035.h4: 1) Supreme Sovereignty — Union of Paradise Deity and the Sevenfold God
12.036.p: The sovereignty of a Creator Son who has completed seven bestowals integrates the seven viewpoints of the Paradise Deities [21:5.2] and the seven creature attitudes of time and space [21:5.3]. This produces a perfected synthesis of Creator will and creature perspective, making this sovereignty inherently supreme [21:5.4]. Such sovereignty encompasses the full divinity of the Sevenfold God and finds its culmination in the Supreme Being [21:5.5].
12.037.h4: 2) Scope of Rule — Absolute Authority in the Local Universe
12.038.p: Master Michael is absolute in his local universe [21:5.8]. Except for matters involving the extinction of will creatures, even the superuniverse authorities do not limit his power [21:5.8]. He maintains continuous contact with every world of his bestowals through his spiritual presence, the Spirit of Truth [21:5.10], and retains unbroken communication with the Eternal Son [21:5.10].
12.039.h4: 3) The Eternal Way — The Way, the Truth, and the Life
12.040.p: Master Michael embodies the realization of Paradise Deity potential within himself [21:6.4]. He is destined to serve as the eternal guide leading all creatures from finite existence toward divine perfection [21:6.4]. His ascent to supreme sovereignty indicates that he now possesses transcendent capacities for service beyond the limits of the finite [21:6.2].
13.title: Thought Adjuster
13.001.h3: 1. Origin and Nature of Thought Adjusters
13.003.p: Thought Adjusters proceed directly from the Universal Father and are not created beings but actual fragments of the Infinite God Himself [107:1.2]. They are undiluted, pure divinity—unconditional and perfect—and in essence, they are God as far as finite beings can perceive Him [107:1.2], 107:1.5. Awareness of the Adjuster’s presence is fundamentally awareness of God’s presence within the human mind [107:0.4].
13.005.p: Although Adjusters are not personalities (pre-personal), they are real, distinct, and fully individualized spirit entities [107:7.1]. They appear to possess will on a pre-personal level [107:7.3], and their mind-nature resembles the combined mind qualities of the Universal Father and Eternal Son [107:5.3]. They are unfailingly perfect in all their ministry and have never erred in any universe assignment [107:4.3].
